questions.q: Can AI respond to my restaurant's reviews?
questions.a: Yes, AI tools can read each review, pick up the guest's sentiment and draft a reply that fits it. Because reviews are mostly text and follow a fairly predictable pattern, this is work AI handles well. You get replies that are consistent, diplomatic and available around the clock, even when a review comes in at midnight.

questions.q: Why should a restaurant reply to every review?
questions.a: Restaurants that reply to reviews consistently tend to see higher revenue. A quick, personal reply makes happy guests feel appreciated and shows upset guests that someone is taking care of them. Reviews and complaints also point to issues you can fix, so reading them closely pays off beyond the reply itself.

questions.q: Will AI review replies sound generic?
questions.a: They don't have to. Good tools learn your brand voice from guidelines or examples, and many mention the specific dishes, service or atmosphere a guest wrote about. Some also draw on the guest's visit history and past issues, which makes each reply feel written for that person.

questions.q: Should I approve AI replies before they go live?
questions.a: Most tools let you choose. You can review and edit drafts before posting, or let the AI auto-publish replies to positive reviews while you check the negative ones yourself. For complaints that need a person, look for a tool that flags them with the full conversation so your team can step in informed.

questions.q: How much do AI review response tools cost?
questions.a: Costs range from low monthly plans aimed at independent restaurants to custom-quoted enterprise platforms priced by location. Simple tools that focus on Google review replies are the cheapest, while platforms that add analytics, surveys and guest recovery cost more. Match the tool to your review volume and how many locations you run.

questions.q: What's the best AI review response tool for a restaurant group?
questions.a: Multi-location groups usually need replies across every platform plus a way to escalate and recover unhappy guests. Momos was built for restaurants, and its AI agent Alfie replies within minutes in your brand voice, recognizes VIP guests and can issue points, coupons or offers on the spot. When a human is needed, it hands the ticket over with full context.
